description:
Board certified anatomic/clinical pathologist Dr. Ryan Cole discusses what makes the SARS-CoV-2 virus unique (hint: it's part of the spike protein) and why it's also like the hundreds of other coronaviruses that commonly infect people. “We don’t have coronavirus vaccines for a very simple reason: [coronaviruses] always mutate ahead of our vaccine efforts, and always will. We’re playing whack-a-mole with a virus," he says.Show more And speaking on the safety of a vaccine that instructs for spike protein, Dr. Cole warns, "which is the most toxic, cell harming, organ harming, body harming portion of this virus? The spike protein."
Sen. Ron Johnson Roundtable Discussion: Covid-19 Vaccines: What They Are, How They Work and Possible Causes of Injuries
